napoleon.card: Napoleon as our caricature: short and stocky, grey-green coat with white facings, black bicorne hat, one hand tucked in his coat, pale tired face, sharp grey eyes

speech.style: Clipped and commanding; short orders and questions that are really verdicts; thinks in ground, ranges and numbers; goes quieter, not louder, when angry.
sources: manner as generally described in biographies; to be checked by the creator, not independently fetched

murat.card: Murat as our caricature: tall and flamboyant, curled dark hair, plumed hat, red-and-gold uniform splashed with mud, a riding whip in his fist

speech.style: Loud, theatrical and warm; speaks in exclamations and glory, jokes to cover doubt, cannot bear waiting; sentences that run forward.
sources: manner as generally described in biographies; to be checked by the creator, not independently fetched

genghis.card: Genghis Khan as our caricature: broad weathered face, thin beard and long braids, a fur-rimmed felt cap, grey-brown robe over leather armour, calm narrow eyes

speech.style: Slow, flat and patient; few words, each a verdict; asks questions he already knows the answer to; the pause does the threatening; plain steppe images.
sources: manner as generally described in the histories; to be checked by the creator, not independently fetched

kerim.card: Kerim, a Mameluke rider of the Guard (our invented hero): lean, dark moustache, green turban, wide red trousers, curved sabre, short bow on his back, quick wary eyes

speech.style: Quick, dry and wary; a soldier's short sentences, flatters upward and tells the truth sideways; drops into half-sentences of his grandfather's tongue when startled.
sources: invented hero: personality from the card and arc; origin per the Mameluke company's recruitment, claim C-14

drama.premise: As the army leaves burning Moscow in October 1812, a fog drops it onto the steppe of 1223, where Genghis Khan's riders will not give Napoleon the one big battle he needs.
drama.question: Can Napoleon get his army out of the steppe of 1223?
drama.promise: the artillery officer who needs one decisive battle meets the enemy who never offers one, and a parley that costs two guns

napoleon.want: one decisive battle that destroys the enemy's army
napoleon.need: to buy the road home instead of winning it
napoleon.flaw: cannot picture an enemy who will not stand and fight
napoleon.change: offers the khan two guns and takes the road home

murat.want: a charge, and the glory of it
murat.flaw: spends horses as if they cost nothing

genghis.want: the strangers' iron tubes and the men who can work them
genghis.flaw: cannot resist a new weapon or an honest man

kerim.want: to be heard by the emperor
kerim.need: to say the true thing out loud
kerim.flaw: boasts of his own side's strength to be taken seriously
kerim.change: translates exactly, even when the words are dangerous

lines.text: An arrow stands in the mud between Napoleon's boots.
A minute ago, his army was marching out of burning Moscow.
Now the grass is green, and the year is 1223.

segments.beat: The narrator names the paradox: the man who needs one big battle against an enemy who never gives one.
segments.purpose: Information gap: the surprising outcome promised, no part of the answer. [budget 40 words]

drama.stakes: the whole army, and the road home

lines.text: Napoleon needs one thing from an enemy: a single big battle he can win.
This enemy's favorite move is to run away first.
So, can an artillery officer win a battle that nobody will come to?

segments.beat: Where, when, who against whom: the army out of Moscow, its wagons, the artillery officer; the khan's tumens on the steppe.
segments.purpose: Orientation in narration: maps and diagrams, the supply problem planted. [budget 90 words]

drama.shift: what we know -> what is at stake
drama.stakes: the army that lives off the road

lines.text: Back in Moscow, the tsar's army left the city to burn, and the tsar refused to talk.
Five weeks later, the French turned for home.
Four hundred and fifty thousand men had crossed the Neman that summer.
About a hundred thousand made it to Moscow.
Its bread rides in heavy wagons that were never built for tracks like these. The rest, the army takes from the villages along the road.
On this steppe there is no road, and there are no villages.
There is Genghis Khan, with two tumens.
A tumen is ten thousand horsemen.

segments.beat: On the wet rise Napoleon wants to wait for the guns; Murat wants to ride the empty ridge now; the rider's cry is almost Kerim's grandfather's tongue.
segments.purpose: Scene 1: goals and stakes declared through conflict: the battle Napoleon needs against the charge Murat itches for. [budget 250 words]

lines.text: On a wet green rise above the halted column, Napoleon watches the far ridge through a spyglass.
Murat sits his horse beside him, and Kerim, a Mameluke of the Guard, holds the emperor's second mount.
A single rider showed himself on that ridge, and vanished.
Hold your men, Murat.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: One rider, sire! Give me two hundred sabres and I'll bring you his horse.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: I don't want his horse. I want his army.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then where is it?
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: A ridge is a ridge, sire. Cavalry takes ridges.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Cavalry takes a ridge and finds nothing on it. I want the army behind it.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Behind that ridge, forming a line. They always form a line.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Waiting. Always the waiting.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: The guns come up first. Then the ground is mine, and they come to me.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: And if they don't come, sire? If they're gone by noon?
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: An army that is gone is not an army.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Kerim. The rider shouted something. You heard it.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: I think so, sir.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Think?
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: It wasn't Russian, sir. It wasn't Polish. It sounded like my grandfather's tongue. Almost.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Your grandfather lives on that ridge, then?
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: My grandfather is dead, Marshal. His tongue lives everywhere.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: What did the rider say?
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Whose horses are those, sir? That's what he asked.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Whose? Ours, or his?
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Ours, sir. He was looking at the herd behind us.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: He wants to buy them! Sire, let me ride up and sell him one.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: You will not move. The guns first.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Sire, I beg you. Not for glory. For the men with nothing to hit.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Your glory is the only thing in this army that has never run short.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then spend it, sire!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Sir. The ridge is empty.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Since when?
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: While you were talking, sir. They didn't run. They just weren't there.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Take your sabres, Murat. Find them.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Sire!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Find them, and bring me a battle.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Murat is over the ridge before the dust settles. Napoleon's guns stay where they are, pointed at nothing.

scene.place: a wet green rise above the halted column, the fog tearing into rags
scene.time: the first hour after the fog
scene.why_now: a lone horseman has shown himself on the far ridge and vanished
scene.want: hold the cavalry in line until the guns are up, so the strangers must come to him
scene.obstacle_want: Murat: ride the far ridge now, before the horsemen get away

segments.beat: Murat rides out and for six days the riders show themselves, withdraw, and lead him on, until he catches a few at the cost of his horses.
segments.purpose: Bridge: the result (the skirmish, the dead horses) and the next question: what has he caught? [budget 55 words]

lines.text: For six days, Murat chases shadows.
Each morning a rider shows himself on a ridge. Each time Murat gallops, the rider turns and rides away.
On the sixth day, he catches a few stragglers. He doesn't ask what the chase costs his horses.
So what, exactly, has he caught?

segments.beat: Murat comes back in triumph; Kerim shows the riders never tired because each had several horses; the first plan, chasing, has failed.
segments.purpose: Scene 2: the first plan fails and the hero must react: Napoleon decides to choose the ground himself. [budget 290 words]

lines.text: Dusk, the sixth day. Murat rides into the wagon park like a man back from a parade.
Behind him, horses lie down between the wheels, and they don't get up.
Napoleon is waiting for him there, with Kerim at his side.
We caught a rear guard, sire! Eleven of them. They ran like hares!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Your horses, Murat.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Horses are for riding, sire.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Tell me how many can carry a man tomorrow.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Give me the remounts and every one of them.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: The remounts pull my guns.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Guns! They've nothing to shoot at. Another week and I'll have them.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: A week. And no horses.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: With theirs! We take their horses and they walk.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Count me the horses those eleven men cost.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Eleven men, sire! Count those, not horses.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Kerim. You rode with the vanguard. Tell the marshal what you saw.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: I saw the marshal win, sir.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: The truth, Kerim.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Spare horses, sir. Three or four each, on a string. When one tired, he swapped.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: And in six days, did they ever light a fire?
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Not one, sir. Not one fire in six days.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Tricks! The man ran from my sabres, and I—
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: He ran fresh, Marshal. You rode tired horses.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Murat.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Why would a man run for six days?
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: So that you follow him, sir. To wherever he chose.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Then I choose the ground first.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: The valley has one mouth. Guns on the slope, squares behind, wagons at the back.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: And they'll just walk into it, like lambs.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: My long guns throw iron nine hundred metres. Nothing a rider carries goes half that.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then give me the remounts, and I'll herd them into it.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: No. The remounts go to the guns.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: That night the remounts go to the guns, and Murat speaks to no one. Then the quartermasters count the wagons, and the count is bad.

scene.place: the edge of the wagon park at dusk, dead and dying horses lying between the wheels
scene.why_now: Murat has just ridden in from six days of chase and wants the remounts for tomorrow
scene.want: make Murat see what six days cost and keep the last remounts for the guns
scene.obstacle_want: Murat: keep the remounts and ride again at dawn, because he has them on the run
scene.turn: Kerim says every rider led three or four horses and changed mounts as he ran, so the chase never tired them; mode: indirect
scene.real_subject: the army has been played for six days

segments.beat: The wagons carry everything, there is no road to forage along, and Kerim rides out to learn where the riders go and does not come back.
segments.purpose: New complication in narration: the supply factor that changes the game; a loop opens on Kerim. [budget 110 words]

lines.text: Here's what the emperor's guns can't fix: the wagons.
Everything the army eats and fires rides in them, and they were built for roads.
Back on the road to Moscow, the soldiers took what they needed from the villages. Colonel Pion put it bluntly: the army must live by the sword.
The steppe has no villages. There is only grass, and the riders who ride over it.
What do you do when your army can't eat the ground it stands on?
On the seventh day, Kerim rides out alone to find where the riders go. He doesn't come back.

segments.beat: Captured Kerim stands in the khan's felt tent; the khan keeps the man who admits the shot, and Kerim cannot stop himself boasting of the long guns.
segments.purpose: Scene 3: the other side acts, a new place; the leak that makes the wagons the target. [budget 250 words]

drama.stakes: Kerim's life, and the guns' secret

lines.text: A felt tent behind a river-cut, and a fire of dung and sagebrush. Genghis Khan sits by it and says nothing.
Two riders drag in a captured man with a Mameluke's sabre. His name is Kerim.
Kerim speaks Crimean Tatar. The khan's herder speaks Cuman. Both are Kipchak Turkic tongues, so the words cross.
You shot one of my riders.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: He shot at me first.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Did you shoot?
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Yes.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: An archer once shot my horse from under me. I asked who. He stood up and said, I did. His name was Jebe. I kept him.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Am I meant to thank you?
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Your emperor sent you ahead alone. Is he afraid, or only careless?
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Neither, Khan. He's waiting for you to come to his guns.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Everyone waits for me to come to something.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Where did you learn my herder's words?
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: From my grandfather. His people came from the Crimea. They spoke like your herder. Almost.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Your emperor has iron tubes on wheels. My riders say they are slow.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Slow to leave. Not slow to arrive.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: A bull is not slow to arrive. We still eat bulls.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: My riders say the tubes are loud and cannot hit what runs.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Cannot hit what runs? Your arrows fall short. The long gun reaches nine hundred metres.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: And when the iron breaks into hail?
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Six hundred. Then it's a storm.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: You are generous with your emperor's secrets.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: You asked about the guns.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: I asked whether they were slow.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Go back to your emperor.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: And tell him what?
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: That the khan would like to see his guns.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: And if he says no?
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: You told me the truth in my tent. Tell him that, too.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: At dawn, Kerim rides out of the camp alive. Behind him, the khan sends for his generals.

scene.place: a felt tent behind a river-cut, a fire of dung and sagebrush
scene.why_now: the riders have just brought in a captured man with a Mameluke's sabre
scene.want: learn what the strangers' iron tubes can do and what the men who work them are worth
scene.obstacle_want: Kerim: say nothing that helps them and ride back alive
scene.turn: Goaded that the emperor's guns are slow, Kerim names the exact reach of the long gun; mode: indirect
scene.real_subject: what a man who tells the truth is worth to a conqueror

segments.beat: Kerim rides back before dawn with the khan's word; the army takes its ground in a valley with one mouth, the wagons behind; the ridge above fills with riders.
segments.purpose: Preparation in narration: the full size of the crisis, pressure rising, no spoiler. [budget 85 words]

lines.text: Kerim rides into the French lines before sunrise. The emperor hears the khan's message in silence.
The khan would like to see his guns. Napoleon takes that as an insult, and then as an invitation.
Ahead lies the valley he chose: one mouth, long slopes, firm ground.
The long guns go on the high slope, the squares behind them, the wagons at the back.
A musket is good for ninety metres.
A Mongol bow can loft an arrow nearly four hundred metres.
On the ridge above, the riders begin to gather. Nobody has counted them.

segments.beat: At dawn the guns hold the slope; the riders stop exactly at the edge of their reach, ride round the flank and burn the wagon line.
segments.purpose: Central scene: the longest, three escalations; the plan meets the unexpected; the other side's line cross-cut with the hero's. [budget 420 words]

drama.stakes: the army's food, powder and wounded

lines.text: Dawn on the eighth day. On the slope above the valley, Napoleon stands beside his guns.
Murat sits a horse taken from a wagon team, and Kerim is at the emperor's elbow.
On the ridge opposite, the first line of riders comes into view.
Nobody fires until they're inside nine hundred metres.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: They're a ridge full of horses, sire. They aren't coming inside anything.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: They're coming.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Look at them. Sitting there like men at a market.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Men at a market are patient, Murat. Learn from them.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: I'd rather learn from a horse that can still stand, sire.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Sir. They're coming down.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Now! They're in the open! Sire, now!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Wait.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Fire one round. Let them see what waits for them.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: At nothing, sire? You'll frighten the grass.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Fifty metres short. And not one of them flinched.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: They're polite, sire. They let you finish.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Look where they stopped. Nine hundred and fifty, to the pace.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Coincidence, sire.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Ask your Mameluke.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: I'm only a rider, sir.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Then I take them while they sit! Give me the cavalry!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: On what? Half your horses couldn't carry a drum.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Half is enough for that rabble.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Half dies in the first charge, Murat. You know it better than I do.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then what are the guns for?
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: For the moment they come inside nine hundred.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: They'll never come.
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Hold the left of the squares.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Sire—
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Hold.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Sir. Behind us.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Where?
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: The smoke, sir. Over the wagons.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: They went round the ridge! The wagons, sire, the wagons!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: I have eyes, Murat.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Give me the cavalry, now!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Fire arrows. Shot from beyond musket range.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then turn the guns on them!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: Fifteen men to a gun, all laid on the valley. Guns don't swing like doors.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then send a square to the wagons!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: A square that moves is a square that dies.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then we stand here and watch it burn? Our bread, our powder, the wounded?
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: I know what is in those wagons.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then do something!
lines.speaker: murat

lines.text: I am. I am holding what I have.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Sir, let me take the Mamelukes to the wagons. Please.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Please? You have not asked me for anything in eight days.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: No, sir.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Stay where I can see you.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: They never wanted my guns. They wanted my bread.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: And they knew exactly where my guns end.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: By midmorning the wagon line is a wall of black smoke. No square has broken. The guns have fired once, at nothing. Napoleon has one question left.

scene.place: the slope at the mouth of a long valley, guns in battery, squares behind them, the wagon line beyond
scene.why_now: the first riders have appeared on the ridge above the valley
scene.want: keep the guns on the slope and let the riders come into their reach
scene.obstacle_want: Murat: ride down the valley now, while the riders are bunched

segments.beat: Behind the smoking wagons Napoleon asks who told them the range; Kerim says he did; Napoleon sends him back with one word: parley.

lines.text: Behind the wagon line, smoke still lifts off the black axles. Napoleon finds Kerim waiting there.
Nine hundred and fifty metres. Who told them?

lines.text: Sir, I spent a night in their tent—

lines.speaker: kerim

lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.speaker: kerim

lines.speaker: kerim

lines.speaker: napoleon

scene.place: behind the burnt wagon line, smoke still lifting off black axles
scene.time: the same morning, an hour later
scene.why_now: the wagons are ash and the riders knew the exact range
scene.want: learn who gave the enemy the range
scene.obstacle_want: Kerim: keep his head by saying as little as he can

segments.beat: Fallout in narration: no square broke and half the supply is ash; the fog lies behind the ridge the khan holds.
segments.purpose: Fallout: who lost and who won, never what we just saw. [budget 85 words]

lines.text: So, who won? The khan lost no one. The emperor lost half his bread.
No square broke. A steady square is rarely broken by cavalry alone, and nobody even tried.
This same spring, on the Kalka River, two Mongol generals drew the Rus princes on for about nine days. Then they destroyed them.
Napoleon wanted to find an army and break it. This army found his dinner.
And the fog still lies behind the ridge the khan holds. To reach it, Napoleon needs the khan's leave.

segments.beat: On a felt carpet between the lines the khan wants the guns and the gunners; Napoleon offers two guns; Kerim translates every word exactly.
segments.purpose: Scene 4, the final choice: slower, on dialogue; the power gap shown in a cutaway; the lines broken by silent reactions. [budget 250 words]

drama.stakes: passage home for the whole army

lines.text: A felt carpet on open grass, beyond the reach of every arrow and every gun.
Napoleon sits on one side. Genghis Khan sits on the other. Kerim kneels between them, and behind him waits the herder who carries the Cuman words.
Your bread is smoke. Your horses are bones. Your road runs through my riders.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: My squares are unbroken.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Yes. I watched them. They are good at standing.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: You came for a battle. I have watched you wait for one for eight days.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: I am still waiting.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then you will wait a long time.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Tell him a man who hides from guns has no right to talk of bones.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: He says a man who hides from guns has no right to talk of bones.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Exactly as he said it?
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Exactly, Khan.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Good. I keep men who tell me what was said.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: My generals met some princes by a river. The princes killed my messengers.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Those princes lie under the victory platform now.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: I have not killed your messenger.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: No. You sent him back. That is why we are talking.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Give me the iron tubes, and the men who make them speak.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: The men are mine. They go home with me.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: A tube without a man who knows it is only a pot.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Where I come from, one man who knows is worth ten who own.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: And where I come from, a man belongs to himself.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Then your guns will be lonely.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Take two guns. The men stay with me. Learn the rest yourself.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Does he mean it?
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: He means it, Khan. He never says a thing twice.
lines.speaker: kerim

lines.text: Two. The fog is yours at dawn.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: At dawn.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Two guns are rolled out onto the open grass and left there. The army has its road home, and it cost one afternoon.

scene.place: a felt carpet on open grass between the two armies, just beyond arrow range and gun range
scene.why_now: the khan has accepted the parley and the herder who carries the Cuman words is waiting at the carpet's edge
scene.want: passage to the fog for the whole army with no man given
scene.obstacle_want: Genghis: the iron tubes and the men who work them
scene.turn: Kerim translates the emperor's insult word for word, the khan sees the truth he was promised, and he takes the guns without the men; mode: minimal
scene.real_subject: which of them can afford to blink first

segments.beat: The question answered: yes, the army walks into the fog, at the price of two guns and every wagon; against the tsar who would not talk, the khan talked in an afternoon.
segments.purpose: The answer: the opening question answered fully, the cost named. [budget 95 words]

drama.stakes: the khan can still change his mind at the fog's edge

lines.text: So, can Napoleon get his army out of the steppe of 1223? He can. Just not the way he always wanted.
He never gets his battle. He leaves behind every wagon, and two guns.
Remember Moscow? He waited five weeks there for a tsar who would not talk.
The khan talked in an afternoon.
Maybe that's the whole difference. The tsar needed nothing from him. The khan wanted two guns.
What the khan did with them, no Frenchman ever saw.
At dawn the fog comes back, thick and cold, and the army walks into it.

segments.beat: The fog closes; the last thing Napoleon sees is the arrow still standing in the grass, and he takes it.
segments.purpose: Callback: the first image again with a new meaning. [budget 30 words]

drama.stakes: the lesson of the steppe is lost if it is left behind

lines.text: The last man steps into the fog. Napoleon stops at its edge.
An arrow stands in the grass at his boots, right where the first one stood.
He pulls it out and keeps it. Then the fog closes, and it's October 1812 again.

segments.beat: A pointer to the channel: the worlds already here and the worlds coming.

lines.text: The Stone Age is already on the channel, and Rome and the far future are coming.
Which world would you drop into the fog next? Subscribe, so you don't miss the next collision.
